rl-ed-def.back: The juncture of two or more different cover types.

rl-ed-ecotone.back: A soft, blended edge: forest and open land mixed through shrubs and young trees.

rl-ed-leopold.back: Interspersion: food and cover types mixed close together, not just more edge.

rl-ed-six.back: Timber and grass, cutblock, burn, field and brush, creek strip, treeline.

rl-ed-distance.front: How far off an edge do beginners sit?
rl-ed-distance.back: 100 to 200 m with a rest and a backstop (Tip).

rl-ed-cutblock.back: Cutblocks by age and Burns by year, with the Satellite base.

rl-ed-downside.back: Predators and other hunters use them too; too much edge hurts some forest birds.

rl-ed-hook.back: Eat in the open, Duck into cover, Go at dusk, Exit at dawn.

rl-ed-rule.back: Do not sit in the field or in the woods. Sit where you can see both.
